title: Stride & Shelf Standup — Nov 04 2026
summary: Weekly standup covering kernel scheduling tweaks ("stride"), KV cache ("shelf") observations, and batching policy experiments. Small perf wins, one infra blocker, action items assigned for canary rollout and eviction investigation.
body:
Meeting: Serving Runtime — Stride & Shelf sync (standing weekly)
Date: 2026-11-04 10:30am PT
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Mei, Ravi, Sofia (+sparse async notes from Anika)

TL;DR
- Kernel scheduling change (PR #8123) reduced short-sequence p95 by ~8% in local pre-prod; canary plan ready for next week.
- KV cache hit ratio improved after LRU->segmented-LRU tweak but saw two eviction storms on Friday that bump cold-start latency. Root cause hypothesis: cohort imbalance + aggressive mem reclaim.
- Batching threshold experiment (E-326) tradeoff: lower CPU but small median latency regression for <64-token requests. Route-based batching policy proposed.
- One infra blocker: intermittent GPU driver preemption during kernel handoff (INFRA-721).

Notes (kernel / "stride"):
- What changed: thread-affinity + adaptive backoff for kernel serial regions (PR 8123). Implementation: pin worker threads for hot kernels, let background eviction threads float.
- Local bench (small sequence profile): baseline p95 42ms -> 38.5ms after change; p50 stable. QPS with synthetic concurrency + short seq improved from 1.2k -> 1.38k per worker.
- Observed: occasional tail spikes at high multi-tenant contended nodes when co-scheduled with long-context jobs. Hypothesis: kernel handoff lock ordering causing priority inversion.
- Decision: roll change to canary at 2% for hostgroup gamma early Monday; metric watch: p99, kernel-lock-wait hist, cpu-steal. If stable after 48h extend to 10% then to 30%. Owner: Liam.
- Follow-up: add lightweight kernel-lock diagnostics (tracepoint) to capture stack traces on >200ms kernel handoff. Owner: Mei. ETA: Tue EOD.

Notes (KV cache / "shelf"):
- Recent tweak: move from simple LRU to two-segment SLRU for hot path. Immediate effect: overall hit ratio +3.2% on paragraph embeddings workload.
- Problem: two eviction storms observed Friday 11/01 at 03:12 and 03:18 UTC affecting region-us-west-2. Symptoms: stepwise increase in cold token latency, cohort-specific cache churn.
- Initial triage: correlates with batch-split spikes (E-326) + background compaction running concurrently. Memory pressure threshold tune was too tight; reclaim triggered aggressive eviction of small-lived keys.
- Temporary mitigation: raise reclaim threshold by 8% on affected pool, stagger compaction windows across pools. Deployed as hotfix with runbook entry. Owner: Ravi.
- Longer term: implement cohort-aware retention policy (keep small request prefixes pinned for 30s). Spec draft in GH issue. Linked: KVC-1914. Owner: Sofia.

Notes (batching / grouping)
- Experiment E-326: increased grouping wait from 8ms -> 12ms to allow slightly larger micro-batches. CPU cost down ~7% for long sequences; median of short requests increased by ~3ms.
- Observation: grouping increase interacts poorly with KV eviction timing (longer grouping delays cause more concurrent live caches -> more pressure).
- Proposal: route-aware batching policy: low-latency routes keep 6ms target, throughput routes use 12ms with adaptive floor. A/B test design discussed. Owner: Priya.
- Action: add a per-route heartbeat metric for avg grouping size and inject into rollout gating. Metric name: route.grouping.avg_size.

Operational items / metrics to watch
- p95 (short seq), p99 (long seq), kernel-lock-wait-95, cache.hit_ratio.by_cohort, route.grouping.avg_size, cpu-steal, mem-reclaim.count.
- Dashboards updated: small update to Serving Runtime -> Kernel -> Canaries to include kernel-lock-wait (Mei).

Blockers
- INFRA-721: intermittent GPU driver preemption during kernel handoff observed on 3 nodes. Infra investigating; root cause unknown. Blocks full canary expansion if root cause not mitigated.
- Dependence on new tracepoint in runtime (needs minor perf vet) to safely capture stack traces. Until tracepoint lands, diagnostics are limited.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Liam: start 2% canary for kernel stride Monday 11/08, monitor 48h. (ETA: 11/08 09:00 PT)
- Mei: land kernel-lock-wait tracepoint + dashboard panel. (ETA: 11/09)
- Ravi: finalize revised reclaim thresholds + stagger compaction hotfix rollout to remaining pools. (ETA: 11/05)
- Sofia: write cohort retention spec (KVC-1914 follow-up) and sync with research for embedding workload patterns. (ETA: 11/12)
- Priya: design A/B for route-aware batching policies and create Linear tickets for canary gating. (ETA: 11/06)
- Anika (async): collect longer-term customer routes to seed route-policy defaults. (no formal ETA)

Open questions / parking lot
- How aggressive should pinned retention be for small prefixes (30s vs 120s)? Tradeoff: memory vs reduced cold-start.
- Should we add per-kernel priority hints from the router (low-latency vs background)? Implementation complexity vs benefit.

Notes to self
- Capture a short runbook snippet for oncall: "If cluster cold-start p95 increases >20% and cache.hit_ratio drops >5% -> check compaction schedule and batching group size changes in last 4h". Add to serving-runtime/ops-runbooks.

References
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/8123
- Jira: KVC-1914 (cohort retention), INFRA-721 (gpu preemption)
- Experiment: E-326 (grouping wait vs cpu tradeoff)

Next meeting agenda (11/11)
- Canary results review (stride roll)
- Deep-dive on eviction storms and compaction interplay
- Draft of route-aware batching rollout plan

End of notes.

Small messy bits: lots of shorthand used above — will convert into polished doc if PR canary is green.
notes_excerpt: Kernel stride PR 8123 good local win; canary planned. KV cache hit +3.2% but eviction storms need cohort-retention fix. Batching grouping tradeoff needs route-aware policy. Infra driver preemption blocks expansion.
